title: Indian audiences in the South and Oklahoma
summary: Welburn asks about Indian listeners; Moore says Indians are mostly in Oklahoma, where they stared at him playing with Ernie Fields.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, in some of the gigs that you played in various parts of the south, did the Indian community come out to the dances, like in Florida, perhaps, or parts of Georgia -- I don't know if you played in parts of Georgia or in Texas -- did the Indian community come out along with the black community and even with some of the whites who would come out to these dances? I was just curious as to how the Indian people may have been interested in this type of music and how you may have met them and so forth. Did they come up and introduce themselves and talk with you?

Well, unfortunately, down south you don't find Indians around. The only place you run into Indians is in Oklahoma. There is an all-Indian town there called Pawhuska and Hominy and all the other places. They seen me up there with Ernie Fields, they'd point at me or they whisper among themselves that I was in there playing with the black men. Otherwise, they like my music, what I did with Ernie Fields. We'll
